sources.title: Repository tagged sorted-array dedupe interview question

claims.text: The preserved source requires duplicate removal from a sorted array with O(1) extra space, without prescribing Java/API/null/tail semantics.

Under the explicit returned-length/valid-prefix contract, the candidate exact Java fence produces the ascending unique prefix for exhaustive and randomized sorted inputs using constant auxiliary state.
The implementation performs one forward read pass with a monotone write index, so time is O(n) and auxiliary space is O(1).

validation.command: extract exact candidate Java; javac -Xlint:all -Werror; compare candidate output prefix to independent TreeSet oracle
validation.reported_stdout: PASS exhaustive=792 random=5000 treeset_oracle=pass extremes=pass null_contract=reject
checks: exact candidate Java compiles with warnings as errors
792 exhaustive sorted arrays match TreeSet oracle
5000 seeded randomized sorted arrays match TreeSet oracle

boundary_tests.expected: return 1 and retain one value in prefix
return n and preserve full array prefix
only prefix nums[0..k) is semantically valid

findings: The preserved repository source says only to remove duplicates from a sorted array with O(1) extra space; it does not specify language, function signature, return value, null behavior, or what must happen to the unused suffix.

The candidate preserves that source boundary and explicitly labels Java int[], returned unique length k, valid prefix nums[0..k), unspecified tail, and null rejection as answer-side contracts rather than source facts.

The read/write invariant is correct for nondecreasing input: before each read step, nums[0..write) is exactly the strictly increasing unique sequence from the scanned prefix; sortedness makes comparison with the last retained value sufficient.
The complete Java class is runnable and uses only fixed scalar state, so the stated O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary-space bounds match the implementation.

Reviewer-owned validation extracts the exact candidate Java fence and compares it against a TreeSet-based oracle over all 792 nondecreasing arrays of length 0..7 over values -2..2, plus 5000 seeded randomized sorted arrays and integer extremes.
Tail contents are correctly excluded from the result contract; no HashSet is used by the candidate itself, and the TreeSet exists only in the independent reviewer oracle.
No fabricated production experience, placeholder implementation, cross-topic contamination, or uncovered source variant was found.
